text.p: Italian bonds and BTP futures held firmer near the day's highs in late afternoon trading boosted by U.S. economic data, a more relaxed view over EMU problems and a firmer lira, dealers said.

They added that U.S. May retail sales showed weaker than expected growth and helped allay fears of a near-term rate rise in the U.S. An OECD outlook report and comments by the Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio had little immediate impact.
"The U.S. data has given all markets a lift, while hopes France can patch up its problems with Europe also gave support," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said that an OECD report issued today that forecast budget deficit/GDP ratios in 1997 of 3.2 percent for Germany, France and Italy compared to a three percent requirement for EMU entry did not unsettle the financial markets.

Fazio said he did not see a near term rate cut in Italy, but this did not surprise a market which no longer looks for an immediate cut in Italian interest rates. Italy's discount rate has been held steady since January despite falling inflation.
Market support came from the firmer lira which gained on the higher dollar, while the trend on most other world bond markets was firmer after the U.S. retail sales figures.
Dealers added that market attention was now focused on Friday's Franco-German meeting in Poitiers in France ahead of the EU Amsterdam summit next week.

French President Chirac said he believed the EMU stability pact could be signed in Amsterdam, despite French Finance Minister Strauss-Kahn's announcement earlier this week that France needed time to study the stability pact.
